extra.message: Insecure pickle deserialization in bundle-thaw endpoint — Remote code execution via a crafted pickle payload. [verified: Duplicate of idx 0 — confirmed pickle.loads on attacker-controlled bytes.]

Arbitrary code execution via eval() on user-controlled expression — Potential remote code execution via Python sandbox escape [verified: eval() with only __builtins__ restricted is a known-incomplete sandbox escapable via object attribute chains on attacker-controlled expr.]

Server-side template injection in jinja-cast endpoint — Remote code execution via template injection payloads (e.g. accessing __class__/__globals__ chains). [verified: Duplicate of idx 1 — confirmed SSTI via unsandboxed Template render of concatenated user input.]

Server-Side Template Injection via Jinja2 render of user input — RCE via Jinja2 SSTI payload (e.g. accessing __globals__/__builtins__ through object attribute chains) [verified: jinja2 Template built by string concatenation of raw GET fragment and rendered unsandboxed; SSTI to RCE.]

Unrestricted file upload via ops drop endpoint — Upload of arbitrary file types/content, potential web shell placement or path traversal via crafted filename [verified: FileSystemStorage.save(drop_blob.name, drop_blob) uses the attacker-supplied filename with no extension/type validation, unlike the properly gated document upload path.]

NoSQL injection in mongo-lane endpoint — Unauthorized enumeration/access of the ops.records collection and potential JS execution via $where depending on MongoDB configuration. [verified: Duplicate of idx 4 — confirmed unsanitized Mongo filter injection.]

XXE via lxml parser with DTD and entity resolution enabled — Local file disclosure, SSRF, or denial of service (billion laughs) via malicious XML [verified: XMLParser explicitly sets load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False and parses raw body — classic XXE with no mitigations.]

Hardcoded fallback Django SECRET_KEY — If deployed without overriding the env var, session/CSRF signing key is publicly known, enabling session and CSRF token forgery [verified: settings.py:6-9 hardcodes a fallback SECRET_KEY used whenever DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset, and this fallback is checked into source control, allowing session/CSRF forgery on any deployment that omits the env var.]

Hardcoded fallback Django SECRET_KEY — Attacker who knows the fallback secret (visible in source) can forge signed session cookies or password-reset tokens for any user, achieving full account takeover including clinic_admin, once a deployment runs without overriding DJANGO_SECRET_KEY. [verified: Same hardcoded fallback SECRET_KEY as finding 0, confirmed present in source at settings.py:6-9 with no forced-random-value mechanism, enabling session/password-reset-token forgery if the env var is omitted.]

DEBUG defaults to True in production — Unauthenticated attackers who trigger any unhandled exception see full Django debug tracebacks leaking source code, local variables, environment/config values, SQL queries, and file paths — a direct path to further compromise of a PHI-handling application. [verified: DEBUG defaults to True per settings.py:11 and .env.example ships DJANGO_DEBUG=1, so an unconfigured deployment leaks full tracebacks including SECRET_KEY and DB credentials on any unhandled exception.]

Hardcoded demo superuser password seeded by management command — Anyone who reads the source (public repo) knows the exact password for the clinic_admin superuser and all seeded patient/clinician accounts; if seed_demo is ever run against a non-throwaway environment, attackers get full admin access to PHI and the Django admin site. [verified: seed_demo.py hardcodes DemoPass123! and applies it via set_password to a real superuser (clinic_admin, is_staff/is_superuser=True) plus clinician/front_desk/patient accounts, with no environment gating preventing execution against non-throwaway deployments.]

Ops module protected only by a single shared static token instead of RBAC — Anyone holding (or guessing/leaking) the one shared token gets unauthenticated access to all ops endpoints including PHI disclosure, RCE via SSTI/pickle, and NoSQL injection. [verified: A single static shared token is the only access control for the entire ops module, with no RBAC/identity binding, unlike access.py's role-based checks used elsewhere.]

Unauthenticated disclosure of sensitive operational data — Unauthenticated attacker can read sensitive business/financial-adjacent data about patients [verified: patient_care_file_072 has no _wrk_gate call at all (confirmed reading the source), unlike every sibling handler, exposing patient_count and ops_memo to anonymous callers.]

Unauthenticated disclosure of sensitive business/patient metadata — Fully unauthenticated attacker can read aggregate patient and business-sensitive metadata. [verified: Duplicate of idx 9 — confirmed missing gate on patient_care_file_072.]
Open redirect in return-lane endpoint — Attacker can craft links that redirect authenticated users to attacker-controlled phishing domains. [verified: Duplicate of idx 10 — confirmed open redirect.]

Mass assignment of privileged fields in workset rebind — Attacker-controlled JSON payload can overwrite privileged fields like role, approved, and balance without any allow-list, enabling privilege escalation or business-logic bypass (e.g. self-approving a workset or elevating role to admin/viewer->staff). [verified: Duplicate of idx 5 — confirmed mass-assignment via workset.update(payload).]

Hardcoded, brute-forceable identity verification codes — Identity-verification bypass via brute force of a 4-digit code space [verified: Static 4-digit codes for two hardcoded handles with no rate limiting are brute-forceable.]

CORS misconfiguration: origin reflection with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can issue credentialed requests to this endpoint and read the response using a victim's session, enabling cross-origin data theft. [verified: Duplicate of idx 7 — confirmed CORS origin reflection with credentials.]

Privilege elevation via forgeable client-supplied cookie/header — Trivial privilege escalation to sensitive payroll/casework data by setting a cookie/header value [verified: Elevated payroll/casework lane is granted purely on an unsigned client-supplied cookie/header value with no server-side verification.]

Insecure-by-default DEBUG and cookie security settings — A deployment that forgets to set the env vars runs with DEBUG=True (verbose stack traces/settings exposure) and cookies sent without the Secure flag over HTTP. [verified: DEBUG, SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE all default to insecure values ('1'/'0') when their env vars are unset, a genuine missing-control default confirmed at settings.py:11 and surrounding cookie settings.]

Non-constant-time comparison of shared internal auth token gating critical RCE endpoints — Timing side-channel to recover the shared token, after which numerous RCE-class endpoints become reachable [verified: _wrk_gate uses plain == on the shared token instead of secrets.compare_digest, a genuine timing side-channel weakness gating many sensitive endpoints.]

Cookie set without Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite flags — Cookie can be exfiltrated via XSS (missing HttpOnly) or transmitted over unencrypted channels/cross-site requests (missing Secure/SameSite) [verified: set_cookie('portal_crumb', marker) is called with no secure/httponly/samesite flags.]

Missing authentication and hardcoded verifier codes on identity endpoints — Unauthenticated attacker can trigger identity/notification actions and brute-force the small hardcoded verifier keyspace (4-digit codes, only two handles) with no rate limiting [verified: Duplicate of idx 14/8 combined — confirmed missing gate plus hardcoded low-entropy verifier codes with no rate limiting.]

Unauthenticated notification-trigger endpoint — Unauthenticated abuse to trigger paging/notification actions for arbitrary handles, enabling spam, harassment, or enumeration. [verified: Duplicate of idx 14 — confirmed missing gate on patient_identity_ping_342.]

Weak PRNG used for security-relevant nonce generation — Predictable nonce/code enables brute-force or prediction attacks bypassing the control it protects [verified: random.choice (Mersenne Twister) is used for a security-relevant code instead of the secrets module used elsewhere in the codebase (ApiKey.issue).]

Weak PRNG used for security-sensitive code generation — Predictable nonce/code values could be guessed or reconstructed by an attacker who observes some outputs, undermining any security use of the value [verified: Duplicate of idx 11 — confirmed weak PRNG for code generation.]

TLS certificate verification disabled on outbound request — A man-in-the-middle attacker on the network path can intercept or tamper with the outbound request/response since certificate validation is disabled [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables cert verification on an outbound request; impact is limited since the target URL is hardcoded, but the insecure pattern is genuinely present.]

TLS certificate verification disabled for outbound HTTPS request — Man-in-the-middle attacker on the network path can intercept or tamper with the outbound request/response [verified: Duplicate of idx 24 — confirmed disabled TLS verification pattern.]

API key accepted via URL query parameter on availability_api — A valid API key transmitted in a URL is far more likely to leak via logs/proxies/history and be reused by an attacker to query provider availability data. [verified: api_key_from_request (portal/access.py:222) falls back to request.GET.get('api_key'), so valid API keys can be passed in the URL and leak via server logs, proxies, browser history, and Referer headers; no mitigating control exists.]

CSV/formula injection in appointment and visit summary exports — A patient-supplied formula payload (e.g. =HYPERLINK(...)) executes when staff open the exported CSV in Excel/Sheets, enabling client-side attacks against clinic staff. [verified: csv.writer writes reason/diagnosis/care_instructions/clinician_notes directly with no leading-character sanitization, and these fields are user-editable text; opening in Excel triggers formula execution.]
